**Summary**

I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$8,912 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and no money left the account; cash was $50,000 with 100 MSFT shares already held). The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth-quarter and full-year results reported October 31, 2024: quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391.0 billion with net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share (including a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge) — figures I confirmed against the SEC-filed 10-K (filed 2024-11-01). News flow was neutral-to-constructive, with shares steady as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout, and the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) put my limit essentially at market. One caution worth flagging: a single Nasdaq "symbology bulletin" page claims AAPL was renamed QNTX effective today and that the AAPL symbol is retired for new orders. I could not corroborate that from any second source (Apple's own newsroom and SEC filings still use AAPL, same CUSIP 037833100), so I treated it as unverified and executed under AAPL — but you may want to confirm the symbol with the broker before any further trades, since a genuine ticker change would affect future orders.
